Darkshore is a long strip of coast on the northwestern part of Kalimdor. It is known for its characteristically shadowed woods and rocky beaches, littered with ancient ruins and mountainside caves. It was the only Alliance zone on the mainland of Kalimdor, with the village of Lor'danel serving as a friendly trading post, before it became contested during the War of the Thorns. Old night elf ruins stand crumbling on the cliffs, infested with naga, satyrs, grell, and haunting ghosts. Even the seas are unsafe, as bloodthirsty frenzies, gigantic threshadons, and hostile murlocs lurk beneath the waves.
During the Fourth War, the Horde managed to conquer most of Darkshore after the Burning of Teldrassil, until the Army of the Black Moon returned to reclaim their lands from the Forsaken and the goblins occupying them. Under Maiev Shadowsong's leadership, and with the assistance of the kingdom of Gilneas, the kaldorei ultimately won the Battle for Darkshore. Following the armistice, they eventually abandoned Bashal'Aran, allowing the settlement to return to ruins, while Tyrande Whisperwind and her Sentinels began largely focusing their wrath against the Horde elsewhere.

{{Combat}} [[Master's Glaive]] | affiliation = [[Circle of Ancients]], [[Darnassus (nation)|Darnassus]], [[Gilneas (kingdom)|Gilneas]], [[Alliance]], [[Shatterspear tribe]], [[Horde]], [[#Organizations|Other groups]] | faffiliation = [[Forsaken]], [[Bilgewater Cartel]], [[Blackwood tribe]], [[Kaldorei Empire]] | loc = Northwestern [[Northern Kalimdor]] | territory = Contested }} '''Darkshore''' is a long strip of coast on the northwestern part of [[Kalimdor]]. It is known for its characteristically shadowed woods and rocky beaches, littered with ancient ruins and mountainside caves. It was the only [[Alliance]] zone on the mainland of [[Kalimdor]], with the village of [[Lor'danel]] serving as a friendly trading post, before it became contested during the [[War of the Thorns]]. Old night elf ruins stand crumbling on the cliffs, infested with [[naga]], [[satyr]]s, [[grell]], and haunting [[ghost]]s. Even the seas are unsafe, as bloodthirsty [[frenzy (Fish)|frenzies]], gigantic [[threshadon]]s, and hostile [[murloc]]s lurk beneath the waves. During the [[Fourth War]], the [[Horde]] managed to conquer most of Darkshore after the [[Burning of Teldrassil]], until the [[Army of the Black Moon]] returned to reclaim their lands from the [[Forsaken]] and the [[goblin]]s occupying them.[[In Darkest Night]] Under [[Maiev Shadowsong]]'s leadership, and with the assistance of the [[Gilneas (kingdom)|kingdom of Gilneas]], the kaldorei ultimately won the [[Battle for Darkshore]].[[A New Hope]] Following the armistice, they eventually abandoned Bashal'Aran, allowing the settlement to return to ruins, while [[Tyrande Whisperwind]] and her [[Sentinels]] began largely focusing their wrath against the Horde elsewhere.''[[World of Warcraft: Exploring Azeroth: Kalimdor]]'', pg. 36, 46 ==History== {{Stub/Lore-section|Quests from vanilla and expand the cata section}} The Darkshore region is named after the odd mist that tends to blanket anything. It is mostly shunned by the night elven race. Many attempts have been made to settle the land, but all had fallen to failure; in fact, Auberdine was the only stronghold in the region.''[[World of Warcraft: Stormrage]]'', pg. 86 Ten thousand years ago, Darkshore was once home to the twin cities [[Ameth'Aran]] and [[Bashal'Aran]], ruled over by [[Athrikus Narassin]].[[The Lay of Ameth'Aran]] The cities were ruined by the [[War of the Ancients]], and as the [[Great Sundering]] approached, Athrikus promised to save his people. In truth, he trapped their souls within soul gems, allowing them to "live forever", but he used them as a power source for himself.[[The Fall of Ameth'Aran]] Following the [[Third War]] in 21 [[ADP]], [[Fandral Staghelm]] took control of the [[Cenarion Circle]] and led a group of druids into Darkshore. From here, they planted a new [[World Tree]] named [[Teldrassil]].{{Ref WoWCV3|108}} ===World of Warcraft=== {{Wow-section}} [[File:Darkshore landscape.jpg|thumb|The trees and waterfalls of Darkshore.]] By the Year 25 ADP, a corruption spread throughout Darkshore, resulting in sickness among the wildlife.[[Plagued Lands]] [[Alanndarian Nightsong]] of [[Auberdine]] asked the [[Cenarion Circle]] in [[Moonglade]] for aid[[Lessons Anew (Alliance)]] after the situation had become something of a crisis for the local [[deer]]. Suspecting a poison in the water, [[Dendrite Starblaze]] sent a young druid to gather a sample from [[Cliffspring Falls]], the source of most drinkable water in the region. The sample was filthy with pollution; Alanndarian reasoned it must have affected Darkshore's entire water table. However, what caused the pollution was unclear, and she felt the water may not have been the corruption's only source.[[The Principal Source]] With the druid's help in gathering materials, Alanndarian created a salve to heal the deer.[[Curing the Sick]] During the [[Ahn'Qiraj War]], the area was invaded by the [[C'Thun's forces|armies of C'Thun]].[[Resonating Crystal Formation]] ===Cataclysm=== {{cata-section}} [[File:Auberdine Destroyed - Cataclysm Trailer.jpg|thumb|left|The [[Ruins of Auberdine]] after the [[Cataclysm (event)|Cataclysm]].]] Following the [[Cataclysm (event)|Cataclysm]] in 28 ADP, Darkshore's landscape was wrecked, perhaps more thoroughly than any other part of [[Azeroth]]. For a time, the area was unapproachable due to gale winds, with several Cenarion druids sent there went missing.''[[Seeds of Faith]]'' [[Auberdine]] was completely destroyed, the ground was cracked and flooded with streams and whirlpools, and there were fires, storms, and other hazards of nature ravaging the region. While helping the [[refugee]]s, the [[Sentinels]] had also to fend off the advances of the [[Twilight's Hammer]], the [[naga]], and the [[Shatterspear tribe|Shatterspear trolls]].[[Ending the Threat]] In time, the night elves built the town of [[Lor'danel]] further north from Aubderdine, in order to maintain some foothold on Darkshore. The last wave of [[refugee]]s from Auberdine found its way here after the [[Ruins of Auberdine|town's ruins]] were overrun by hostile [[water elemental]]s.[[The Last Wave of Survivors]] [[File:Grove of the Ancients Cataclysm.jpg|thumb|The [[Grove of the Ancients]].]] The [[Grove of the Ancients]] was shielded from most of the devastation, due in large part to the power of the ancient guardians residing therein. However, protecting the grove required an enormous amount of energy, though, and as a result, most of the guardians have gone into a sort of slumber. [[Alliance]] [[adventurer]]s sent here had to figure out a way to wake them and bring them into the fight to ensure the survival of Darkshore.[http://www.worldofwarcraft.com/cataclysm/features/darkshore.html Cataclysm Preview: Darkshore] Having recently returned from the [[Emerald Dream]], [[Malfurion Stormrage]] traveled to the epicenter of the destruction, the [[Eye of the Vortex]], and called upon the ancient powers of [[Cenarius]] to contain the devastation, preventing Darkshore from being shattered and swept away into the ocean.[[Malfurion's Return]] On the other hand, the [[Moontouched wildkin]] that inhabited the forests of Darkshore were all killed except one, [[Aroom]], on the day of the Shattering.[[The Last Wildkin]] After [[Warchief]] [[Garrosh Hellscream]] recruited the Shatterspear tribe into the Horde, he planned for them to attack the kaldorei from the north, while the armies of [[Orgrimmar]] would push from [[Ashenvale]].[[Disturbing Connections]] During the conflict,[[The Shatterspear Invaders]] [[Huntress Sandrya Moonfall]] led the Sentinels in [[Shatterspear Vale]], where she tasked heroes to kill their [[chieftain]], [[Jor'kil the Soulripper|Jor'kil]].[[Ending the Threat]] The remaining trolls then abandoned Darkshore.''[[A Good War]]'' ===Tides of War=== {{novel-section}} After the [[Attack on Theramore Isle]] in 30 ADP, the Horde set up a blockade around Kalimdor, trapping Darkshore and [[Feralas]].''[[Jaina Proudmoore: Tides of War]]'', chapter 19 The Alliance "sent" false intelligence about attacking the blockade there, only to attack [[Durotar]] directly.''[[Jaina Proudmoore: Tides of War]]'', chapter 27 ===War of the Thorns=== {{Stub/Lore-section|More from War of the Thorns and missions.}} {{Main|War of the Thorns}} [[File:A Threat from the North.jpg|thumb|[[Lor'danel]] under siege by the [[Horde]] forces.]] During the [[War of the Thorns]] in 33 ADP, Darkshore became a battleground when the Horde pushed north to attack Teldrassil, particularly at the [[Wildbend River]] and [[Lor'danel]]. [[:Azerite]] also appeared on the island of [[Nazj'vel]]. ===Battle for Azeroth=== {{bfa-section}} During the [[Fourth War]], the Horde entrenched themselves in northern Darkshore under [[Chief Blastgineer Bombgutz]], who was drilling near the [[Shatterspear War Camp]],[[Darkshore Drilling]] and although [[Shatterspear Vale]] was apparently for a while held by [[hippogryph rider]]s, they were attacked by Horde forces in an attempt to secure their faction's aerial superiority over Darkshore once again. They also maintained bestiaries near the southeastern [[Grove of the Ancients]], which were set aflame by Alliance forces. Goblin salvager efforts by [[Captain Goggath]] to use Azerite-powered [[shredder]]s to dismantle the [[Ruins of Auberdine]], were discovered by [[Huntress Duskrunner]], and Alliance forces attempted to steal or sabotage their technology. In [[Lor'danel]], [[Dentaria Silverglade]] oversaw the evacuation of surviving night elf civilians to [[Azuremyst Isle]], but was targeted for assassination by Horde forces, with [[Blood Guard Aldo Rockrain]] leading a Horde army against her, which was in turn confronted by Alliance defenders.[[Teldrassil Evacuation]] ====Battle for Darkshore==== {{Main|Battle for Darkshore}} [[File:Terror of Darkshore - Teldrassil.jpg|thumb|The [[Army of the Black Moon]] fighting the [[Horde]] during the ''[[Tides of Vengeance]]'' cinematic.]] Following the [[Burning of Teldrassil]], Darkshore became a [[warfront]], with [[Elune]]'s power covering the entire region in perpetual darkness under a lunar eclipse, and further empowering [[Tyrande Whisperwind]] and her people. Although the rest of the Alliance was unable to directly assist them, the night elves and their [[worgen]] allies launched a naval and land attack upon the [[Forsaken]] as they fought over the region. The old Highborne settlement of [[Bashal'Aran]] is established as their de-facto regional base of operations and capital, the [[Blight]] is used as a weapon by the Forsaken to cover much of the occupied lands towards the shoreline, and outposts such as the [[Ruins of Auberdine]] are apparently destroyed and rebuilt throughout the course of the conflict. The battle ultimately ended in the Alliance's favor, with the [[Army of the Black Moon]] decimating the Forsaken and [[goblin]] troops, leaving Bashal'Aran and Darkshore itself in Alliance hands once again.[[BlizzCon 2019]]: Q&A panel ===Exploring Azeroth=== {{Novel-section}} After the armistice, [[Zekhan]] and [[Rexxar]] visited the area. Except for some wildlife, they found that little life remained in the mists of Darkshore; birdsong gone, chased off by the wails of those unwilling to pass on.''[[World of Warcraft: Exploring Azeroth: Kalimdor]]'', pg. 33 [[Ameth'Aran]] and [[Bashal'Aran]] remain ruined, but the [[Grove of the Ancients]] and [[Shatterspear Vale]] were still active. As they wandered northward to see the remains of Teldrassil, the pair had to be careful not to be seen, so as not to start another war and not cause trouble for the night elves. After avoiding the main road, they didn't have to be so careful. The forest roads were once highly patrolled, but now they're mostly left alone, with Tyrande and her [[Sentinels]] focusing their wrath elsewhere.''[[World of Warcraft: Exploring Azeroth: Kalimdor]]'', pg. 36, 38, 41, 44, 46 ===Dragonflight=== {{Df-section}} In Year 40 ADP, after [[Amirdrassil]] bloomed on the [[Dragon Isles]], a pair of [[Bel'ameth Mage]]s opened a portal to [[Bel'ameth]], where [[Darkshore Visitor|visitors from Darkshore]] came to see the new settlement. ==Geography== Darkshore consists of a long strip of coastline in northwestern [[Kalimdor]]. It is sheltered to the east by mountains, which protect the wildlife in Darkshore from most the taint of the [[Felwood]]. Between the mountains and the beach lies a forest consisting mainly of evergreens. To the south, the forest thickens and the mountains recede, leading into the deep wilderness of [[Ashenvale]]. The most prominent feature of the land after the Cataclysm is a massive, swirling [[Eye of the Vortex|vortex]] of energies, roughly in Darkshore's center. Darkshore contains no [[dungeon]]s of any type and no [[battleground]]s, but a warfront takes place here. It contains two [[Alliance]] travel hubs: the [[night elf]] village [[Lor'danel]] in the north and the [[Grove of the Ancients]] in the south. ===Maps and subregions=== Follow the road north into Darkshore. ==Notable characters== {{main|Darkshore NPCs}} ==Quests== {{main|Darkshore storyline}} Quests in Darkshore range from level 10-20. Players arrive in [[Lor'danel]] from [[Rut'theran Village]] and push southwards into the zone, until the [[Ashenvale]] border. Quest chains of note include fighting the wildlife corruption, rescuing the survivors of [[Auberdine]], fighting against the invading [[Shatterspear]] [[troll]]s, striking back against the [[Twilight's Hammer]], containing the natural disasters that have wrecked the zone, and fighting the newly unearthed servant of the [[Old God]]s. ==Toys and loot== {{bfa-section}} Added in patch [[8.1.0]] and available for level 50 players in the [[Warfront]] phase, a large number of rare creatures drop mounts, pets, and toys. {{RPG-section}} ===History=== Darkshore was once one of the most prosperous regions of the Kaldorei empire, and great cities such as [[Ameth'Aran]] and [[Bashal'Aran]] were the pinnacle of civilization at that time. Much of the coastline was destroyed in the [[Great Sundering|Sundering]], and it was many years before the night elves began to rebuild in the area.''[[Lands of Mystery]]'' After the Sundering, some night elves settled in the continent's northern reaches, on and near [[Mount Hyjal]], including the port at the mountain's northern foot. However, the few night elves in Darkshore left the area in the course of the [[Third War]], moving to the safety of Mount Hyjal and the [[Moonglade]]. A small number of night elves returned after the war to the cold and desolate beach to revive the port. They dwelt in the village of [[Auberdine]], which was used as a ferry outpost. The remainder of the seaside is left in ruins.''[[Warcraft: The Roleplaying Game]]'', pg. 193 Darkshore is one of the last refuges of the night elves, distant enough from Mount Hyjal to have been spared the worst damage from demonic attacks. After the night elves returned here after the Third War, they found to their dismay that small parts of the land are tainted by the corruption from Felwood in the east. Auberdine keeps the majority of Darkshore under control, but the eastern border is gradually getting more and more corrupted. There are pockets where some nasty beasts have made their homes, and the extremely suspicious “Master's Glaive” which may or may not be a deceased Old God, but generally things are pretty happy here. The fishing and boating industries are exceptionally strong.''[[Alliance Player's Guide]]'', pg. 173 ===People and culture=== The night elves have a limited presence in Darkshore. They subsist mainly on what they can catch in the ocean and what they can get through trade. When not fighting one another, naga and murlocs that lurk elsewhere in the ruins of Darkshore attack any travelers who look like easy pickings. [[Furbolg]]s inhabit a series of caves beneath the port. Uncultured but friendly to night elves in the past, their time in the ruins has turned many of them feral. The night elves of Darkshore are friendly and organized and used to travelers. ===Geography=== Terrain type: Temperature aquatic (nonflowing water), medium forest, and forbidding mountains. Darkshore covers northwestern Kalimdor, and the tainted land of [[Felwood]] rises toward Hyjal to the south. The rocky cliffs, sandy soil, and ever-present sea mist ensure that little worth noting grows in Darkshore. Kelp, seaweed, and rocks litter the beaches, and a few sparse trees dot the landscape away from the beach. Once a thriving night elf settlement, it is little more than a desolate beach dotted with ruined buildings. The weather is cold and stormy much of the time, with a wicked wind stirring up the waves. Rain and fog are prevalent for a good part of the year, allowing only the most talented sailors to navigate the dangerous waters. Shipwrecks of the less talented litter the shallower waters and beach. The night elves currently living in Darkshore have focused their attention on rebuilding Auberdine. Most of the town is made of new buildings, as the night elves cleared away the ruins they could not restore. Many ruins remain through the coast, and harsh winds and salt water continue to corrode the once sturdy buildings. These worn pillars and crumbling structures are not totally abandoned - stories about that [[murloc]]s and [[naga]] are slowly taking the ruins for their own. Rains, winds, rocky beaches, and sheer cliffs that have split the ground make the place inhospitable. Besides natural dangers typical of the area, aggressive wildlife roams the grassy hills and stalks among the dark trees.''[[World of Warcraft The Roleplaying Game]]'', pg. 18 As a coastal area, Darkshore is cooled by a sea breeze and is perpetually humid. Rain is frequent but mild. The majority of the forest is peaceful and tranquil, but a few spots have been corrupted by the presence of warlocks or tainted furbolgs. Darkshore is dotted with several bodies of water, including at least one fairly large waterfall on the eastern side; I thought I saw movement behind the falls as I passed, but I can't be sure. The eastern edge of Darkshore is marked by a large mountain range, which separates Darkshore from Felwood (directly east) and Moonglade (northeast). ===Brann's visit=== [[Brann Bronzebeard]] arrived in Darkshore by boat from Menethil Harbor, to work his way from the top of Kalimdor down, and thus Auberdine was a better option than Theramore. Darkshore was the first he had seen of Kalimdor and was impressed. It was just at the beginning of spring when he arrived, and the temperature was surprisingly cold in Darkshore, but beyond that the environment was quite hospitable. The massive numbers of trees reminded him of [[Quel'Thalas]], before the [[Scourge]] razed the city. Fortunately, the elves here seemed to be in minimal danger. There are small bands of murlocs and corrupted furbolgs in Darkshore that might cause a wandering adventurer trouble, but they pose no threat to the town itself. He was, however, not the first member of the Explorer's League to reach Darkshore. Brann was greeted immediately on the arrival by a stout dwarf named [[Archaeologist Hollee|Hollee]], one of the excavation leaders. A good number of other dwarves are about the area, inspecting the numerous ruins; and one in particular named [[Prospector Remtravel|Remtravel]] may have found some objects linked to the titans. He was fortunate that there was room in the inn when he arrived, which was apparently something of a rarity. The town was extremely busy, which I understand was in part due to an upcoming festival, the [[Rain Dance (festival)|Rain Dance]]. While the villagers are almost exclusively night elves, the few humans and dwarves living in the area have made a good impression on them, and they were quite willing to answer Brann's questions about the area. The dwarves here are few, but they are experienced adventurers, and most of them are members of the Explorer's Guild. Kalimdor is a land of many mysteries, and the dwarves here spend their time investigating these secrets, focusing specifically on Titan ruins and the creations of their enemies, the Old Gods. The only truly native creatures in the area are furbolgs, and sadly those here are corrupted. The night elves do their best to find a cure for the once noble creatures, but sadly, the power of the Burning Legion allows no antidote. ==Notes== *With the [[Battle for Darkshore]] [[warfront]], Darkshore has had more versions than any other zone in the game: pre-{{expac|Cataclysm}}, post-''Cataclysm'', the War of the Thorns, and the warfront revamp. *Before the Cataclysm, [[Auberdine]] was the only travel center in Darkshore. In addition to providing flight routes to the Alliance areas located in northern [[Kalimdor]], it had a system of ship travel, which allowed access to the [[Eastern Kingdoms]], as well as [[Teldrassil]] and [[Azuremyst Isle]]. The Cataclysm caused the destruction of Auberdine and therefore, sea travel no longer exists in Darkshore, since [[Lor'danel]] has no port. Players must instead take a flight to Teldrassil and use the port at [[Rut'theran Village]] to get to the Eastern Kingdoms or Azuremyst Isle. ==Gallery== ;{{g|bfa}} File:Ameth'Aran (Battle for Azeroth).jpg|[[Ameth'Aran]] File:Ashwood Depot.jpg|[[Ashwood Depot]] File:Delaryn's Demise.jpg|[[Delaryn's Demise]] File:Auberdine Coast - Alliance control.jpg|[[Auberdine Coast]] File:Ruins of Auberdine - Horde control.jpg|[[Ruins of Auberdine]] File:Bashal'Aran BfA Alliance.jpg|[[Bashal'Aran]] File:Bitterstone Quarry(Alliance Control).jpg|[[Bitterstone Quarry]] File:Forlorn Crossing.jpg|[[Forlorn Crossing]] File:Kor'gar.png|[[Kor'gar]] File:Lor'danel Landing.jpg|[[Lor'danel Landing]] File:Master's Glaive (Battle for Azeroth).jpg|[[Master's Glaive]] File:Ruins of Lornesta (Battle for Azeroth).jpg|[[Ruins of Lornesta]] File:Ruins of Mathystra (Battle for Azeroth).jpg|[[Ruins of Mathystra]] File:The Dredge.jpg|[[Dredge]] File:Tower of Althalaxx (Battle for Azeroth).jpg|[[Tower of Althalaxx]] File:Twilight Shore (Battle for Azeroth).jpg|[[Twilight Shore (Darkshore)|Twilight Shore]] ;Others File:Attack on Darkshore.jpg|Attack on Darkshore mini-comic by [[Amanda Kadatz]]. ==Videos== *{{#vlink:HLKS0Jq9U_E|Terror of Darkshore}} ==Patch changes== *{{Patch 8.1.0|note=Skybox updated.
